summary.headline: Sigma Advanced Systems Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to INR417 crore (about 12% QoQ) with 19.7% operational EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance INR1,900-2,000 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR417 crore in Q2 FY27 versus INR374 crore in Q1, with operational EBITDA of INR82.28 crore (19.7% margin) against INR61 crore in Q1. Profit after tax excluding associate share was INR48.6 crore versus INR35.41 crore in Q1. Management tied the step-up to UK integration (Nasmyth, Bromford), the Sri City facility starting production in September, and defence export shell orders. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and announced plans for a fundraise of up to INR3,000 crore to fund acquisitions, with closings targeted around Q4.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR374 crore in Q1; about 11-13% QoQ as stated
Q1 margin not stated in call

financial_highlights.value: About INR80 crore (term loan INR76 crore)

segments.name: UK aerospace (Nasmyth, Bromford)
segments.commentary: Management says UK EBITDA margin improved at least 200 bps per quarter from Q3 FY26 to Q2 FY27 after about GBP 8-9 million of investment in capex, buffer stock and supply chain. On-time-in-full rose from 65% to about 97%. UK execution growth guided at 15-20% YoY.

segments.name: Defence exports (artillery ammunition)
segments.commentary: Export shell and fuse orders are expanding. Management said about 85% of the M107 export order revenue was recognised in Q1 and Q2, with the remaining 15% completing in October and reflecting in Q3. Margins improved as more production was insourced to Sri City.

segments.name: Domestic defence and electronics
segments.commentary: Domestic is about 3-4% of mix per analyst question, and about 10% of revenue per management. Counter-drone Indrajal Ranger received Government of India orders, with a large BSF contract under MHA in execution. Defence electronics currently runs single shift.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target close to INR1,900-2,000 crore with about 20% EBITDA margin.
EBITDA margin improvement of 200-400 bps by end FY27 and a further 400-600 bps by end FY28, from transferring work to India.
Management said FY28 aerospace EBITDA margin could reach 25-30%, and consolidated margin in line with Indian peers in FY28.
Sri City Phase 1 utilisation targeted at 50-60% by end FY28, with full utilisation in FY29.
Management said Q3-Q4 will carry most of the ramp-up from aerospace and defence exports, with about INR2,700 crore of defence export order book.
Acquisitions targeted at companies with USD100-150 million revenue; closings expected around Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Sri City facility commenced production in September 2026; parts already shipping from India to the UK.
Management said there is no further capex planned as capacity is in place; aerospace capacity utilisation in India about 15% and ammunition about 20%.
Current CCT utilisation 10-15%, expected to rise about 10 percentage points every quarter (per management answer).
Work split guidance: about 30% of transferred work retained in UK, about 70% moved to India.
UK automation (palletisation) investment aimed at 24/7 machine running and operational margin gains.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR10,000 crore plus, of which about 90% is international; defence export order book about INR2,700 crore.
Announced new orders of INR3,915 crore from July 1 to date (per management).
Management said NATO and allied nations are increasing ammunition capacity; NATO order book opened and new NATO customer discussions ongoing.
Aerospace order book described as executable with 5-7 years visibility; UK customers have contracted backfill commitments.
About 90% of revenue export-driven, all in GBP, USD and EUR; management declined to give customer-wise order breakup.
Management said Sigma sells directly to defence primes and aerospace majors (Rolls-Royce, Airbus, BAE Systems, Lockheed Martin), not to sub-tiers.

qa_highlights.question: Investment in Nasmyth and Bromford post-acquisition, and drivers of margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About GBP 8-9 million invested in working capital, buffer stock, new equipment and insourcing. OTIF improved from 65% to about 97%. UK EBITDA margin improvement expected to continue quarterly as new kit ramps.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose and timing of the INR3,000 crore fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily to fund acquisitions; closings expected around Q4. Management said no working capital raise is needed and the fundraise is subject to shareholder approval.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 155mm shell and fuse orders for the full shell?
qa_highlights.answer: Announced orders are for individual components: filled fuses and shell bodies are separate orders. Sigma can supply the whole shell except explosive. Shell forgings are bought in; the rest of production is in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue recognised on the M107 export order and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 85% recognised in Q1 and Q2; remaining 15% completed in October and will show in Q3. Defence export margins expanded QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and repayment plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described debt as about INR80 crore, mostly working capital. The INR76 crore term loan repayment is not yet decided. Other term borrowings are scheduled to amortise from January to December 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow statement line for bank balances other than cash equivalents?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said these are the preferential-issue proceeds parked in fixed deposits pending deployment.

risks_watch: Guidance depends on a sharp H2 ramp: management needs roughly INR1,200 crore of revenue in H2 to reach the INR1,900-2,000 crore target, versus about INR800 crore in H1.
Acquisition-led growth: a roughly INR3,000 crore fundraise and planned Q4 deals carry integration and execution risk. Management said deal targets are USD100-150 million in revenue.
Margin expansion depends on transferring UK work to India (30:70 split) and on UK automation, both still in progress.
Management said the UK P&L will run through Sigma UK, so India-plant margin gains will show only in consolidated numbers.
Restatement risk: management said not all aerospace revenue and margins are fully disclosed and declined to give FY28 breakdowns.
Watch Q3 for recognition of the remaining 15% of the M107 order and the first quarterly progress against the 200-400 bps margin target.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on order book, margins and the UK turnaround. Evasive on customer-level order splits, FY28 breakdowns, acquisition targets and the fundraise size and mix. Several answers were repetitive or unclear on the audio.
key_quotes: What made the quarter exceptional was the new order wins from our acquisition, which consolidates our leading position in aerospace and wings.
We're in a very unique position, being an Indian player focused on exports.
Our order book as on date is about 10,000 plus crores. Out of which 90% is international, giving us a very strong long- term visibility.
So, the fundraise is primarily to fuel our growth coming in from M&A, new acquisitions.

adds.what: Sri City facility (Phase 1) commenced production; parts already shipping from India to UK

growth.why: FY27 guided to INR1,900-2,000 crore (~20% EBITDA margin), backed by a INR10,000 crore+ order book and INR2,700 crore defence export book, but no capacity additions beyond Sri City Phase 1 (already live) and no revenue-growth percentage stated, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: by end FY27; further by end FY28
rows.why: Operational EBITDA margin 19.7% in Q2 vs INR61 crore EBITDA in Q1 (about 16% on INR374 crore), with management targeting 200-400 bps improvement by end FY27 and a further 400-600 bps by FY28 from shifting work to India (30:70 split) and UK automation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 (live); Phase 1 full ramp by FY28
rows.why: Sri City Phase 1 commenced production in September 2026 and parts are already shipping to the UK; utilisation targeted at 50-60% by end FY28, with 10-15% today and management guiding about 10 points a quarter.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR1,900-2,000 crore needs about INR1,200 crore in H2 versus about INR800 crore in H1, backed by a INR10,000 crore+ order book and INR2,700 crore defence export book, though India aerospace utilisation is only about 15%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said no further capex is planned because capacity is in place; aerospace utilisation in India is about 15% and ammunition about 20%, so utilisation does not point to a new capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,900-2,000 crore on INR800 crore in H1 and announced INR3,915 crore of new orders since July 1, but it still needs a sharp H2 ramp, so an upgrade is conditional.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs about INR1,200 crore of revenue against INR800 crore in H1, and margin gains depend on work transfer and UK automation that are still in progress.

rows.label: INR3,000 crore fundraise for acquisitions
rows.why: Management plans a fundraise of up to INR3,000 crore, subject to shareholder approval, to fund acquisitions of USD100-150 million revenue companies, while saying no working capital raise is needed.

rows.label: Defence export order conversion and NATO demand
rows.why: About 15% of the M107 export order is due to be recognised in October (Q3), and the INR2,700 crore defence export book plus NATO order book opening support further orders.

rows.label: UK margin improvement from automation and insourcing
rows.why: UK EBITDA margin has improved at least 200 bps per quarter since Q3 FY26 after about GBP 8-9 million of investment, with OTIF up from 65% to about 97%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the UK turnaround, margins, order book and Sri City ramp, but evasive on customer-level order splits, FY28 breakdowns, acquisition targets and fundraise size; analysts pressed on the H2 revenue ramp and on the fundraise.
